name: Deuruxolitinib
lead: Deuruxolitinib (brand name Leqselvi; formerly CTP-543) is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor approved in the United States for adults with severe alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition that causes patchy to total scalp and body hair loss.[1] It is a deuterated form of a JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor, and in vitro assays reported in the US label showed greater inhibitory potency for JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 than for JAK3.[1]

Its efficacy was tested in the Phase 3 THRIVE-AA1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adults aged 18 to 65 with at least 50 percent scalp hair loss, which was published in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology in 2024.[2] Systematic reviews of JAK inhibitors in alopecia areata describe the class as producing meaningful regrowth while raising safety questions that include infections, acne and laboratory changes.[3][4]

The US label carries a boxed warning covering serious infections, mortality, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events and thrombosis.[1] The drug is a prescription medicine for a medical condition; discussion of it in appearance communities is tied mainly to hair regrowth in alopecia areata rather than to pattern hair loss.

paras: The US label lists deuruxolitinib for adults with severe alopecia areata and states it is not recommended in combination with other JAK inhibitors, biologic immunomodulators, cyclosporine or other potent immunosuppressants.[1] It is not indicated for androgenetic (pattern) hair loss.

THRIVE-AA1 enrolled adults with at least 50 percent scalp hair loss and compared oral deuruxolitinib with placebo; its authors reported significant hair regrowth in the treated groups.[2] Network meta-analyses and systematic reviews comparing JAK inhibitors in moderate-to-severe alopecia areata place deuruxolitinib among the newer agents with positive randomized data.[3][4][5] Reviewers note that most evidence concerns short randomized periods and that relapse after stopping JAK inhibitors has been described across the class.[3][6]

The most common adverse reactions listed on the US label (at least 1 percent) include headache, acne, nasopharyngitis, increased blood creatine phosphokinase and hyperlipidemia.[1] A meta-analysis of placebo-controlled trials of JAK inhibitors in dermatology found an increased risk of acne as an adverse event.[7]

The boxed warning describes increased risk of serious infections including tuberculosis, mortality, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events and thrombosis.[1] The label also lists gastrointestinal perforation, lipid elevations, anemia, neutropenia and lymphopenia among warnings, and states that the drug is contraindicated in CYP2C9 poor metabolizers and in people taking moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors.[1] Based on animal studies, the label states it may cause fetal harm.[1] Systematic reviews of JAK inhibitor safety in alopecia areata report mostly mild adverse events in trials but note limited long-term data.[8][9]

JAKs mediate signaling of cytokines and growth factors important to immune function; JAK inhibitors block this signaling, which is thought to interrupt the immune attack on hair follicles in alopecia areata.[1][3] Deuruxolitinib is deuterated, a modification intended to alter its metabolism.[1] Dedicated phase 1 studies examined its pharmacokinetics in renal and hepatic impairment.[10][11]

THRIVE-AA1 (NCT04518995) is the pivotal Phase 3 trial in adults.[2] Further registered trials include a Phase 3 study in adolescents with severe alopecia areata (NCT07133308) and a Phase 3 study in Japanese adults (NCT07617597), both recruiting.[12][13] Review articles summarize the broader JAK inhibitor evidence in alopecia areata.[3][4][14]
No forum material on deuruxolitinib was available for this article. It is a newly approved prescription therapy for an autoimmune hair loss condition.

timeline.event: Phase 1 studies of renal and hepatic impairment pharmacokinetics begin.[10][11]

card.summary: Newly approved oral JAK inhibitor for severe alopecia areata, with strong regrowth data and a boxed warning.
card.note: Prescription drug with boxed warning (infections, cardiovascular events, thrombosis, malignancy); indicated for alopecia areata, not pattern baldness.

quick.overview:
Deuruxolitinib (Leqselvi) is an oral prescription pill approved in the US for adults with severe alopecia areata, an autoimmune cause of hair loss.

In a Phase 3 trial, adults with at least half of their scalp hair lost regrew significantly more hair on the drug than on placebo. It is not approved for male or female pattern hair loss.
quick.mechanism: It blocks Janus kinase enzymes, which relay inflammatory signals; this is thought to reduce the immune attack on hair follicles.
quick.risks: The label has a boxed warning for serious infections, death, cancer, heart events and blood clots. Common effects include headache, acne and raised cholesterol. It is contraindicated with certain CYP2C9 conditions and may harm a fetus.
